title: Advanced Practices & Smells
objectives: Restrain macro usage to real wins
body:
# Advanced Practices & Code Smells

## unsafe: minimal surface, maximal documentation

```rust
/// Splits `buf` into fixed chunks. SAFE because:
/// - pointer stays within allocation (len % CHUNK == 0 enforced)
pub fn chunks(buf: &mut [u8]) -> ChunksMut<'_> {
    // one unsafe block at most, with invariant comment
}
```

Rules of thumb: smallest possible unsafe region; a comment naming the exact
invariant; a safe wrapper as the only public path; tests (and Miri when
targets support it) exercising edge cases. If you cannot state the invariant,
you are not ready to write the unsafe block.

## Macros earn their keep rarely

Good uses: repetition, DSL-lite literals (`json!`, `vec!`), deriving boilerplate.
Bad uses: hiding control flow, imitating functions with side effects, saving
three keystrokes. If plain generics/fns/closures solve it, skip the macro.

## Smell: pointer soup

```rust
// BAD: what owns what?
struct Widget { children: Rc<RefCell<Vec<Rc<RefCell<Widget>>>>> }
```

**Why:** ownership graphs unreadable; leaks via cycles; panics from borrow()
at runtime.
**Refactor:** restructure so parents own children (`Vec<Widget>`), pass
`&mut` where needed, reserve Rc cycles for genuine graph domains (then use
Weak back-references deliberately).

## Smell: macro-generated public APIs without docs

Expansion hides behavior. Document the macro itself with doctests showing the
expanded usage — future readers cannot step into your macro easily.

## Memory debugging toolkit

`cargo clippy` catches layout footguns; Miri (nightly) interprets code catching
UB in unsafe; valgrind/heaptrack profile allocations. In this app's capstone
you will wire diagnostics display — reuse that UI to teach these tools.

exercise.prompt: 🐞 Bug hunt: this API hands out raw indices and silently misindexes (y*width bug). Fix `get` bounds-checking BOTH axes and print Some(6)/None cases for (2,1) and (3,0) on a 3x2 grid filled row-major 1..=6.
hints: Row-major index is y * width + x.
Bounds-check x < width AND y < height before computing.
